title: Mandan calls Dec. 15 special election on large-scale AI data center ban
source_used: Dakota News Network (9 Oct 2026) plus the visible lede and teaser of The Bismarck Tribune (7 Oct 2026)
key_facts: Mandan, North Dakota, will hold a special election on Dec. 15 on whether to ban large-scale data centers.
The vote is in addition to next month's midterm election.
The city verified a citizen petition (Bismarck Tribune teaser: 'Voters to decide Dec. 15 after the city verified a citizen petition').
A second special election, to replace commissioner Craig Sjoberg who died in August, has no date yet and will likely be in the new year.
The Tribune photo caption places the City Commission meeting on Tuesday (6 Oct 2026).
quote_evidence: In addition to next month's midterm election, Mandan will hold a special election on December 15th, when voters will decide whether they want to ban large-scale data centers.
Mandan voters will decide whether to ban large-scale data centers in a special election set for Dec. 15.
why_it_matters_hint: Voters in a small city decide directly whether large AI data centers may be built.
notes: Bismarck Tribune body is scrambled for non-subscribers and was not decoded; only the plain lede, caption and teaser were used, plus the full Dakota News Network item. Details of the proposed ban are not in the text used.
